background: Nationwide Building Society is the largest building society in the world and the UK's second-largest mortgage lender, a mutual funded by retail savings and current accounts and lending mainly on residential mortgages, now also the owner of Virgin Money.
synthesis: The society is rated A+ on average across all three main agencies, all three on a stable outlook, with the last move a two-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026. Capital is mixed against UK building societies: CET1 of 18.6% is above the peer median, but leverage of 5.2% is in the bottom quarter, the figure to watch. Liquidity is also mixed, with LCR of 174% below the peer median and NSFR of 145% level with it. None of the ratios has moved materially over the past four periods (figures to 30 Jun 2026), and nothing has been flagged in the last 90 days.
